chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn (both), from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah, from his father (peace be upon them both), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) gave the two grandmothers one-sixth, provided there was no mother below the maternal grandmother, and no father below the paternal grandfather.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: These two narrations are not acted upon, because the first narration is disconnected (mursal) in its chain, and the second, along with the first, contradicts what we have previously presented of narrations, because we have clarified that the grandmother is only entitled to the share from the portion of her child. The narration also implies that she is given the share if there is no child of hers there, and it is possible that the two narrations came as a place of taqiyyah (dissimulation), because Abu Bakr ruled by this in his caliphate, so it is permissible that it was narrated according to what he ruled.

key_terms.مُرْسَلٌ: disconnected narration (missing a link in the chain)

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance share of a grandmother in Shia fiqh and why are some narrations about it not acted upon?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* records the Prophet granting one-sixth to grandmothers when their direct descendants are absent, a ruling distinct from the standard principle that a grandmother inherits only from her child's share. Shaykh al-Tusi notes the chain is disconnected (*mursal*) and the content contradicts established juristic consensus, suggesting the discrepancy may stem from *taqiyyah* or the precedent set by Abu Bakr’s caliphate.
